title: Atlas: Hierarchical Partitioning for Quantum Circuit Simulation on GPUs
problem: Efficient partitioning and simulation of quantum circuits across distributed GPUs requires minimizing inter-GPU communication costs while exploiting available parallelism. Larger quantum circuits exceed single-GPU memory capacity, necessitating distributed simulation strategies.
motivation: Efficient quantum circuit simulation at scale is essential for quantum algorithm development and validating quantum computing systems.
method: Atlas partitions quantum circuits hierarchically into subcircuits for multi-GPU execution. An Integer Linear Program formulation optimizes placement to minimize communication by mapping nearby gates to nearby GPUs. Dynamic programming determines the optimal subcircuit assignment to GPU kernels. For larger circuits, data is offloaded to DRAM to extend capacity.
key_novelty: Hierarchical circuit partitioning combined with Integer Linear Programming to minimize communication in distributed quantum circuit simulation on GPUs.
contributions: Hierarchical partitioning framework for scalable quantum circuit simulation
Integer Linear Program formulation for communication-aware subcircuit placement
Dynamic programming algorithm for GPU kernel assignment optimization
Atlas implementation achieving 2x speedup over existing GPU simulators and 100x improvement for large circuits via DRAM offloading

metrics.speedup: 2x over GPU-based simulators on average; 100x over large-circuit simulators

primary_theme: Hierarchical quantum circuit partitioning for multi-GPU simulation
